pathway.title: CENTENE CORP — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: First, Centene has reduced debt materially: total debt was USD 15,542 million at September 30, 2026 against USD 17,401 million at December 31, 2025, the 2027 notes, carried at USD 2,211 million at year-end, fell to USD 568 million at September 30, 2026, and the remainder was redeemed in October 2026 (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Debt register, Chart data: debt maturities; CP-1A Timeline). The mechanism is note repurchases funded by cash and by a USD 970 million receivable sale, and the implication is that no scheduled note maturity falls before 2028 on the CP-1 register.

Second, leverage looks sound on last-twelve-month figures but less so on the quarterly shape. Calculated total debt over EBITDA is 3.62x, against 2.98x for FY2024 and 6.86x for FY2025, and EBITDA over cash interest paid is 6.85x (Analyst Interpretation on an analyst-defined EBITDA; CP-1 Chart data: leverage and interest cover). Calculated EBITDA was USD 2,568 million in Q1 2026, USD 1,933 million in Q2 2026 and USD 325 million in Q3 2026, and Medicare Advantage earnings are front-loaded by the issuer's own account (Management Language; CP-1A Company and operating model, Seasonality). A creditor should therefore treat 3.62x as a ceiling on comfort until fourth quarter results confirm the recovery.

Third, parent liquidity is the binding constraint. Consolidated cash of USD 20,700 million sits mostly in regulated subsidiaries, unregulated cash is USD 376 million, and USD 175 million is available for general corporate use; management expects only about USD 20 million of net insurance-subsidiary dividends for the rest of 2026 (Documentary Fact and Management Language; CP-1 Liquidity at September 30, 2026; CP-1A Company and operating model, Subsidiary dividends). Debt service therefore rests on the undrawn USD 4,000 million revolver and on dividend capacity that state regulators control, with interest paid of USD 627 million over the last twelve months.

Fourth, reported cash flow overstates recurring generation. Nine-month operating cash flow of USD 4,287 million includes net receivable sale proceeds of USD 970 million, and Q3 2026 operating cash flow was an outflow as state pass-through payments were paid through (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Reported cash flows, Narrative review). Free cash flow of USD 3,943 million over the last twelve months should not be read as a recurring figure.

Fifth, business risk is driven by government payors and dated regulatory change. Medicaid was 57% of FY2025 external revenues, Florida and New York each exceed about 10% of Medicaid premium revenues, certain Hawaii Medicaid contracts and the Florida Children's Medical Services contract were lost, and Texas and Georgia protests are open (Documentary Fact; CP-1A Company and operating model, Concentration and Contract renewal risk). Marketplace membership fell to 3,403,300 from 5,828,100, 2027 Star Ratings cover about 42% of Medicare Advantage membership at 3.5 stars or higher against about 60%, and California and Medicaid work-requirement changes take effect in 2027 and 2028 (Documentary Fact; CP-1A Timeline, Credit translations). Revenue and margin visibility into 2027 and 2028 is therefore lower than the 2026 recovery suggests.

Sixth, the covenant has wide stated room but cannot be verified. Issuer debt to capital is 41.1% against a 0.60 to 1.00 maximum, and the issuer states compliance (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Covenants as disclosed), but the agreement's definition, guarantors and any restrictions on distributions are not supplied, so covenant headroom is Not calculable and legal capacity is not assessed (Insufficient Information).

runs.text: Strengths. Scale and diversification across Medicaid, Medicare, Commercial and Other, with Medicaid in 30 states and Medicare Advantage in 32 states, spreads exposure across many payors even though two states are material (Documentary Fact; CP-1A Company profile, Company and operating model). Deleveraging is real and documented: debt of USD 15,542 million, debt to capital of 41.1% against 46.5% at December 31, 2025, and the 2027 notes cleared (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Reported balance sheet, Debt register). Liquidity at the parent is supported by an undrawn USD 4,000 million revolver with no letters of credit against it, maturing March 5, 2030 (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Liquidity at September 30, 2026). Interest cover has recovered to 6.85x from 3.92x on an analyst-defined EBITDA (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 Chart data: interest cover). Documented management behaviour is creditor-supportive, with note repurchases, no common stock repurchases in Q3 2026, no sponsor and no documented value extraction (Analyst Interpretation on documented actions; CP-1A Governance and issuer behaviour). The medical cost position improved on a nine-month basis, with a health benefits ratio of 89.9% against 91.1% a year earlier (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Financials and credit metrics; CP-1A Credit translations).

Weaknesses. Earnings are volatile and front-loaded: calculated EBITDA fell to USD 2,535 million in FY2025 from USD 6,213 million in FY2024, and was USD 325 million in Q3 2026 (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 Financials and credit metrics, Narrative review). Parent cash is thin relative to USD 15,542 million of debt, and upstream dividends are regulator-controlled (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Liquidity at September 30, 2026). The business depends on government rate setting and procurement, with dated headwinds in 2027 and 2028 (Documentary Fact; CP-1A Company and operating model, Timeline). Cash flow is distorted by pass-through timing and a receivable sale that carries repurchase obligations under the agreement, which is not supplied (Documentary Fact and Insufficient Information; CP-1A Conflicts logged). Documentation gaps limit the view: covenant definitions, indentures, guarantors and the Magellan sale agreement are Not supplied (Insufficient Information). A Securities Action alleging false statements about 2025 guidance is pending, with no loss estimate and accrued amounts described as not material (Management Language; CP-1A Governance and issuer behaviour).

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: There is no sponsor, acquisition or leveraged buyout in the supplied sources, and no new debt was issued in 2026. The cash flow statement shows no proceeds from long-term debt in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, against 750 in the same period of 2025 (CP-1). The transactions that matter to a creditor are three. First, the pending sale of the remaining Magellan Health businesses, agreed in December 2025: its buyer, price, expected closing date and use of proceeds are Not supplied, and held-for-sale assets and liabilities of 312 each are on the September 30, 2026 balance sheet. Second, the February 13, 2026 master receivable purchase agreement with MUFG Bank, Ltd. for up to 4,250 of 2025 plan year stand-alone Part D risk-sharing receivables: a participating interest of 1,000 was sold in March 2026 for net proceeds of 970, which funded part of the redemption of the 2027 notes, with 3,250 of purchase capacity remaining at September 30, 2026 and settlement of the sold interest expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. Third, debt reduction through the senior note repurchase program, whose authorization was raised in February, May and October 2026, and the October 2026 redemption in full of the remaining 569 of 2027 notes; this is a subsequent event after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet. The credit agreement dated March 5, 2025, with a revolver of 4,000 and a term loan, is described in the 2026 filings without any amendment. The next scheduled note maturity on the debt register in CP-1 is the 2028 notes. Terms of the agreements are Not supplied, so legal capacity, baskets and covenants are not assessed here.

fields.value: - Strongest contrary evidence: the debt and covenant mechanics sit in filing summaries and not in the executed credit agreement or indentures, which are listed only as exhibits (10-K FY2025 page:180: "4.4 Indenture, dated as of February 13, 2020, by and between Centene Corporation, as issuer, and The Bank of New York Mellon Trust"). The risk mechanism is that a consumer may read the issuer's debt-to-capital ratio as a covenant test when the credit agreement's own definition is not available, which would mis-state covenant headroom in CP-2.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Second mechanism: the Part D receivable sale is accounted as a sale, so the receivable leaves the balance sheet and the cash proceeds are operating cash flow (Q3 10-Q page:14: "The cash proceeds and associated loss on sale of receivables are recorded as operating cash flows."). A consumer that reads operating cash flow without this note would overstate organic cash conversion, which CP-1 and CP-2 must separate from the sale.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Third mechanism: the Magellan businesses are held for sale, so segment and consolidated trends include a perimeter that is leaving (Q3 10-Q page:13). CP-1A must keep that perimeter visible.

On the analyst-calculated EBITDA used throughout (the issuer reports none), LTM leverage to September 30, 2026 is 3.62x and LTM cover of cash interest is 6.85x, against 6.86x and 3.92x for FY2025, when the health benefits ratio rose to 91.9% from 88.3% in FY2024. Three cautions control the read. Earnings are front-loaded, so the LTM ratios are better than the third quarter run rate. fields.value: - Leverage: total debt fell from 17,401 to 15,542 between December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2026, and the analyst-calculated LTM ratio is 3.62x against 6.86x for FY2025. Mechanism: the FY2025 ratio was inflated by lower earnings, since the health benefits ratio rose to 91.9% from 88.3% in FY2024 (EBITDA already adds back the impairment), while 2026 repurchases of 1,847 par of the 2027 and 2028 notes reduced the numerator. Implication: leverage has returned toward the FY2024 level of 2.98x but is not yet there, and it rests on an earnings recovery that is not evenly spread across the year.

Implication: the LTM ratio overstates the run rate that the second half implies; the creditor should watch fourth quarter results before treating 3.62x as stable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CENTENE CORP is a publicly listed, widely held managed care organization with no sponsor, controlling owner or leveraged transaction in the supplied sources. Its credit-relevant facts are operating and regulatory. Revenue comes mainly from state Medicaid agencies and from the federal government through Medicare and the Marketplace, so margin is the spread between premium set by payors and medical costs, which the issuer measures as the health benefits ratio. Membership of 25,698,200 at September 30, 2026 was below the 27,968,100 of a year earlier, driven by a Marketplace decline, while stand-alone Part D membership grew. The record shows a company that spent 2026 reducing debt, repricing the Marketplace and absorbing severance costs, while facing dated regulatory changes in 2027 and 2028. The corporate transactions in the record are small relative to the group: the pending Magellan Health sale, a receivable sale facility with MUFG Bank, Ltd., and note repurchases. No new debt was issued in 2026. Ownership above the filings, board composition and the terms of the sale and financing agreements are Not supplied, so sponsor behaviour is judged on documented actions only and legal capacity is not assessed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: Medicaid was 57% of FY2025 external revenues; Florida and New York are each about 10% or more of Medicaid premium revenues (10-K FY2025 page:13, page:15); the Florida CMS contract concluded and Hawaii contracts were not renewed (Q3 10-Q page:37). Mechanism: premiums and contracts are set by a small number of public payors through rate cycles and procurements, so a single loss or rate shortfall changes revenue and margin quickly. Implication: revenue is large but not locked in; the creditor should weight procurement outcomes and rate adequacy ahead of absolute scale. Countering fact: new and renewed contracts, for example Illinois beginning January 2027 (Q3 10-Q page:37).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: health benefits ratio of 91.9% for FY2025 against 88.3% for FY2024 and 92.7% in Q3 2026 after 87.3% in Q1 (10-K FY2025 page:107; Q1 10-Q page:32; Q3 10-Q page:40). Mechanism: with medical costs the dominant cost line and premiums fixed for the year, a small ratio drift removes most of the margin, and Medicare costs rise through the year as deductibles are met. Implication: LTM measures in CP-1 are flattering relative to the second half; monitor fourth quarter results and the 2027 rate cycle. Countering fact: the nine-month ratio of 89.9% was better than 91.1% a year earlier (Q3 10-Q page:42).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Regulatory and eligibility risk. Evidence: OBBBA work requirements and funding changes, expiry of enhanced Marketplace subsidies and a fall in Medicare Advantage Star Ratings coverage to about 42% of membership in plans rated 3.5 stars or higher from about 60% (Q3 10-Q page:30, page:31, page:38). Mechanism: eligibility and subsidy changes reduce membership and raise morbidity before rates adjust; lower Star Ratings flow into 2028 plan year revenues. Implication: expect membership and revenue pressure through 2027 and 2028 with an uncertain timing of rate offsets. Countering fact: the dual-eligible integration rule from 2030 favours Centene's overlapping Medicaid and Medicare footprint, as management states (Q3 10-Q page:32), which is Management Language.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Sponsor alignment and creditor control. Evidence: no sponsor; documented debt reduction and a pause in repurchases (Q3 10-Q page:21, page:46). Mechanism: with dispersed ownership, capital allocation is decided by the board and constrained by covenants not supplied. Implication: documented behaviour is creditor-supportive, but this is not a contractual protection. Counter: the receivable sale facility with repurchase obligations (see conflicts).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Centene is a large, government-funded health insurer whose credit quality improved in 2026 but remains sensitive to medical costs and regulation. The strongest support is deleveraging: total debt fell to USD 15,542 million from USD 17,401 million, calculated leverage on last-twelve-month EBITDA is 3.62x against 6.86x for FY2025, and a USD 4,000 million revolver is undrawn. The weakest point is earnings stability and parent-level cash: calculated EBITDA was USD 2,568 million in Q1 2026 but USD 325 million in Q3 2026, and cash available for general corporate use was USD 175 million. What decides the outcome is whether the health benefits ratio holds through the fourth quarter and the 2027 rate cycle while Marketplace, Medicaid and Star Ratings changes take effect.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Thesis (Analyst Interpretation): Centene has repaired its balance sheet faster than its earnings are proven, so the credit is improving but depends on a stable health benefits ratio and on rate and regulatory outcomes that are outside its control. Basis: CP-1 leverage and quarterly EBITDA shape; CP-1A Credit translations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, Centene has reduced debt materially: total debt was USD 15,542 million at September 30, 2026 against USD 17,401 million at December 31, 2025, the 2027 notes, carried at USD 2,211 million at year-end, fell to USD 568 million at September 30, 2026, and the remainder was redeemed in October 2026 (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Debt register, Chart data: debt maturities; CP-1A Timeline). The mechanism is note repurchases funded by cash and by a USD 970 million receivable sale, and the implication is that no scheduled note maturity falls before 2028 on the CP-1 register.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second, leverage looks sound on last-twelve-month figures but less so on the quarterly shape. Calculated total debt over EBITDA is 3.62x, against 2.98x for FY2024 and 6.86x for FY2025, and EBITDA over cash interest paid is 6.85x (Analyst Interpretation on an analyst-defined EBITDA; CP-1 Chart data: leverage and interest cover). Calculated EBITDA was USD 2,568 million in Q1 2026, USD 1,933 million in Q2 2026 and USD 325 million in Q3 2026, and Medicare Advantage earnings are front-loaded by the issuer's own account (Management Language; CP-1A Company and operating model, Seasonality). A creditor should therefore treat 3.62x as a ceiling on comfort until fourth quarter results confirm the recovery.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third, parent liquidity is the binding constraint. Consolidated cash of USD 20,700 million sits mostly in regulated subsidiaries, unregulated cash is USD 376 million, and USD 175 million is available for general corporate use; management expects only about USD 20 million of net insurance-subsidiary dividends for the rest of 2026 (Documentary Fact and Management Language; CP-1 Liquidity at September 30, 2026; CP-1A Company and operating model, Subsidiary dividends). Debt service therefore rests on the undrawn USD 4,000 million revolver and on dividend capacity that state regulators control, with interest paid of USD 627 million over the last twelve months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth, reported cash flow overstates recurring generation. Nine-month operating cash flow of USD 4,287 million includes net receivable sale proceeds of USD 970 million, and Q3 2026 operating cash flow was an outflow as state pass-through payments were paid through (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Reported cash flows, Narrative review). Free cash flow of USD 3,943 million over the last twelve months should not be read as a recurring figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fifth, business risk is driven by government payors and dated regulatory change. Medicaid was 57% of FY2025 external revenues, Florida and New York each exceed about 10% of Medicaid premium revenues, certain Hawaii Medicaid contracts and the Florida Children's Medical Services contract were lost, and Texas and Georgia protests are open (Documentary Fact; CP-1A Company and operating model, Concentration and Contract renewal risk). Marketplace membership fell to 3,403,300 from 5,828,100, 2027 Star Ratings cover about 42% of Medicare Advantage membership at 3.5 stars or higher against about 60%, and California and Medicaid work-requirement changes take effect in 2027 and 2028 (Documentary Fact; CP-1A Timeline, Credit translations). Revenue and margin visibility into 2027 and 2028 is therefore lower than the 2026 recovery suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sixth, the covenant has wide stated room but cannot be verified. Issuer debt to capital is 41.1% against a 0.60 to 1.00 maximum, and the issuer states compliance (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Covenants as disclosed), but the agreement's definition, guarantors and any restrictions on distributions are not supplied, so covenant headroom is Not calculable and legal capacity is not assessed (Insufficient Information).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Scale and diversification across Medicaid, Medicare, Commercial and Other, with Medicaid in 30 states and Medicare Advantage in 32 states, spreads exposure across many payors even though two states are material (Documentary Fact; CP-1A Company profile, Company and operating model). Deleveraging is real and documented: debt of USD 15,542 million, debt to capital of 41.1% against 46.5% at December 31, 2025, and the 2027 notes cleared (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Reported balance sheet, Debt register). Liquidity at the parent is supported by an undrawn USD 4,000 million revolver with no letters of credit against it, maturing March 5, 2030 (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Liquidity at September 30, 2026). Interest cover has recovered to 6.85x from 3.92x on an analyst-defined EBITDA (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 Chart data: interest cover). Documented management behaviour is creditor-supportive, with note repurchases, no common stock repurchases in Q3 2026, no sponsor and no documented value extraction (Analyst Interpretation on documented actions; CP-1A Governance and issuer behaviour). The medical cost position improved on a nine-month basis, with a health benefits ratio of 89.9% against 91.1% a year earlier (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Financials and credit metrics; CP-1A Credit translations).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Earnings are volatile and front-loaded: calculated EBITDA fell to USD 2,535 million in FY2025 from USD 6,213 million in FY2024, and was USD 325 million in Q3 2026 (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 Financials and credit metrics, Narrative review). Parent cash is thin relative to USD 15,542 million of debt, and upstream dividends are regulator-controlled (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Liquidity at September 30, 2026). The business depends on government rate setting and procurement, with dated headwinds in 2027 and 2028 (Documentary Fact; CP-1A Company and operating model, Timeline). Cash flow is distorted by pass-through timing and a receivable sale that carries repurchase obligations under the agreement, which is not supplied (Documentary Fact and Insufficient Information; CP-1A Conflicts logged). Documentation gaps limit the view: covenant definitions, indentures, guarantors and the Magellan sale agreement are Not supplied (Insufficient Information). A Securities Action alleging false statements about 2025 guidance is pending, with no loss estimate and accrued amounts described as not material (Management Language; CP-1A Governance and issuer behaviour).
